To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Monday Embakasi briefing: casual pay and Kisumu loads

Brian,

For your Sunday read-through. This is a working draft for Monday morning; please don’t circulate it more widely before I’ve reviewed it. I’ll be travelling, but I’ll be up from 4:30. WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes.

First: go in calm, direct and accountable. This is our mess, not theirs. The casuals did nothing wrong. Don’t go in defensive, and don’t suggest they caused the delay by raising concerns. Some have rent due on the first; take that seriously.

What happened with Friday’s pay

The bank rejected the bulk payment file on Friday. The file had 212 records, but the beneficiary reference in column 7 was too long for the bank’s new template, introduced after its 25 November platform upgrade. The bank confirmed that none of the payments in that file were processed. The rejection alert went to the old Finance mailbox and was only seen after 5pm, when the bank cut-off had passed. That means the Friday transfers did not go through. It was a processing failure on our side, and management should own it plainly.

Finance has approval to pay the affected casuals by M-Pesa instead. The realistic timing Kevin gave us is Monday by 11am. That is the time we can communicate; it is not a guarantee that everyone will see funds earlier. Don’t say “by lunch,” “in a few minutes,” or give anyone an individual time we haven’t confirmed. We learned in Mombasa in 2024 what happens when a supervisor gives a time we can’t keep. We must not repeat that.

What you can tell them

Management has approved KES 500 per head for Monday lunch and fare for every casual on the affected list. These amounts will be paid in the same M-Pesa batch as the delayed pay. M-Pesa charges are paid by the company and will not be deducted from anyone’s payment.

Peninah has confirmed 198 phone numbers. She’ll be at Embakasi from 7:30 with the list and a printout. She could not reach 14 people, mostly new loaders from the Athi River intake. She’ll check those numbers face to face and can print payslips for anyone who wants one. Please don’t describe the 14 as refusing to respond or as holding up the other payments. Help Peninah find them and pass on corrected numbers promptly. Don’t promise a precise payment time for an individual whose number still needs checking.

You can say the approved plan is an M-Pesa batch, with the current expectation that money will be on phones by 11am Monday. If the batch or timing changes, say so honestly and promptly. Don’t imply the bank processed Friday’s file, or that the whole group has already been paid.

How to speak with the group

Please apologise in person on management’s behalf. Keep it simple: “Friday’s pay did not go through because our payment file was rejected under the bank’s new template. We didn’t catch the alert in time, and we should have. None of you caused this. We’re correcting it by M-Pesa, with the current expectation that it will reach phones by 11am Monday. The approved lunch and fare amounts are included in the same batch, and the company is covering the charges. Peninah is here to help check numbers and print payslips.”

Listen before you try to settle the room. Don’t argue over whether people have a right to be upset, and don’t use phrases like “you’ll just have to wait.” If you don’t know an answer, say you’ll check and come back with it. Don’t fill a gap with a guess. Ask Peninah or Kevin to confirm details rather than improvising.

Speak with Ouma privately before addressing the whole group if you can. He is loud, but he is not a bad man; he has four children and rent to meet. Give him a chance to explain what people are worried about, acknowledge the impact, and share the confirmed plan. Don’t treat him as the problem or make an example of him in front of everyone. Then speak to the group together, with Joseph and Peninah available to help.

If the Kisumu loading is refused

The Kisumu trucks need to leave by 9am to make the mill’s offloading slot. That is important, but it does not change what we can promise about pay, and it is not a reason to pressure people with threats. If Ouma’s group says they will not load, stay calm. Do not threaten anyone’s contract, dismissal or future shifts. No one is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day.

Work stoppages are not the grievance channel. The procedure says grievances go first to the shift supervisor, then to HR within 48 hours. Any stoppage must be handled jointly by Operations and HR. So involve Joseph and HR immediately; don’t try to resolve or discipline the group alone. Ask what would help them feel heard, restate the verified payment plan, and give them a clear route to raise individual pay or payslip questions with Peninah and any wider grievance through Joseph and HR. Keep the conversation respectful and avoid escalating it into an argument.

Do not promise a workaround, extra payment, or a revised departure time unless it has been authorised and confirmed. Keep Operations and HR together on any response to a refusal, record the key facts and what was said, and update me if the situation changes. If loading cannot proceed, escalate through the joint Ops/HR process rather than making threats or trying to force a resolution on the spot.

Please keep the message consistent: own the mistake, give the 11am expectation without dressing it up as a guarantee, explain the approved lunch and fare support, and make space for people to be heard. I’ll be reachable before the 7:05 flight.
